description: Everything the oracle replaces. Only the GPU, the clock, transports and external services may be replaced; check_mocks.py fails if an entry names decision code.

mocks.how: constructed by the harness instead of by a model runner: each scheduled request that reaches the end of its known tokens samples its next assigned output token from the scenario
vLLM's own CPU test helper builds the real Scheduler with a fixed KV capacity (num_blocks) and a 1-head, 1-dim float32 full-attention spec, so no tensors are allocated; it is called, not modified

the assigned output's last token is sampled as EOS_TOKEN_ID (tests/v1/core/utils.py:43), so the simulator's output-length input ends the request through vLLM's own check_stop; max_tokens carries only a client budget
oracle/run_metrics.py only: time.time and time.monotonic read the virtual clock (the step index), so the scheduler's event timestamps are deterministic; no decision reads them in the scenarios run
oracle/run_metrics.py only: IterationStats' iteration_timestamp reads the virtual clock (the step index), so latency series are deterministic; they are derived families and not compared

oracle/run_metrics.py only: EngineCoreEvent timestamps (QUEUED, SCHEDULED, PREEMPTED) read the virtual clock (the step index), so the queue-time series is deterministic; a derived family, not compared

constructed by the harness instead of by a drafter: after each step that ran, every request in it is proposed num_speculative_tokens draft ids and handed to Scheduler.update_draft_token_ids, as EngineCore.post_step does (vllm/v1/engine/core.py:689-696); only the count reaches a decision

a verify step samples one token plus the scenario's accepted count for that request and step (at most the drafts it verified; a placeholder -1 draft is always rejected, rejection_sampler.py:762-763): acceptance is an input (#2021 B3), the rejection algorithm is outside parity

the helper's VllmConfig is called with vLLM's own SpeculativeConfig, LoRAConfig and KVEventsConfig built from the scenario (oracle/run_scheduler.py build_scheduler); a speculative draft is a configuration-only checkpoint under oracle/drafts (architecture, no weights); vLLM derives every value the scheduler reads

the helper's SchedulerConfig is called with the scenario's watermark, max_num_active_seqs, max_num_scheduled_tokens and long_prefill_token_threshold_adaptive, which the helper fixes (watermark=0.0) or does not expose

DSpark scenarios only: set True with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1, as on a GPU host, so vLLM accepts the DSpark config (it runs only on the V2 model runner, vllm/config/vllm.py:2976-2979); the Scheduler class and its decisions are the same on either runner

with kv_events on, the scheduler's null publisher object's publish method is wrapped to keep a copy of each step's KVEventBatch (scheduler.py:2371-2385) for the trace; the events themselves are vLLM's

hybrid scenarios only (kv_groups): the helper's KVCacheConfig is called with one layer per group built from vLLM's own FullAttentionSpec and SlidingWindowSpec (1 head, 1 dim, float32, as the helper's single group), each sliding-window layer tagged with extra_retained_tokens = num_prefill_lookahead_tokens - 1 read from the built VllmConfig, as get_kv_cache_configs tags it at launch (vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:2582-2589); and with disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager the layers pass through vLLM's own unify_hybrid_kv_cache_specs first; vLLM's KVCacheManager picks the coordinator and per-group managers

oracle/run_enginecore.py only: execute_model and sample_tokens return futures that resolve, when the batch queue pops them, to the shared GPU mock's ModelRunnerOutput; which requests sample is read from the scheduler's own is_prefill_chunk when the batch executes

oracle/run_enginecore.py only: EngineCore.__init__ (vllm/v1/engine/core.py:118-259) loads a model and profiles a GPU, so the EngineCore is built with object.__new__ holding the real scheduler and the attributes __init__ would set (batch_queue_size = VllmConfig.max_concurrent_batches, the deque, no structured output, no spec decode); step_with_batch_queue and step run unmodified

oracle/run_enginecore.py only: the CPU platform turns async scheduling off (vllm/platforms/cpu.py:329-331); the scenario's value is set back after it ran, with the scheduler class get_scheduler_cls() picks for it

oracle/run_enginecore.py only: the V2 model runner needs Triton, which the CPU wheel lacks (inference-sim/blis-vllm#3), so the scenario's choice is passed to create_scheduler and to VllmConfig.max_concurrent_batches' own code, as vLLM's own CPU tests do (tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py:499-517)

oracle/run_dp.py only: the DP process group's all-reduce is answered with the sum it would compute over the ranks' votes of this step (any rank has unfinished requests); DPEngineCoreProc._has_global_unfinished_reqs runs unmodified, as vLLM's own tests script it (tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py:641-657)

oracle/run_dp.py only: the coordinator's [waiting, running, kv_cache_usage] publication reaches the client every stats_interval steps and stats_lag steps late, from the ranks' own counts; DPLBAsyncMPClient.get_core_engine_for_request runs unmodified on a client holding exactly the state it reads (tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py:208-222)

oracle/run_dp.py only: the client is built with object.__new__ holding exactly the state get_core_engine_for_request and process_engine_outputs read (client_count 1, the in-flight maps, one engine identity per rank, the rotating start, a config naming the V1 runner and allgather_reducescatter), as vLLM's own tests build it (tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py:208-222@5df63a72); the method runs unmodified. The finished-request bookkeeping is process_engine_outputs' own two lines (core_client.py:1703-1710), applied by the harness when a request finishes

oracle/run_dp.py only: each rank's DP engine core is built with object.__new__ holding exactly the state _should_throttle_prefills and _has_global_unfinished_reqs read (dp_group, dp_sync_interval, prefill_schedule_interval, step_counter, current_wave, pending_pause, ignore_start_dp_wave, engines_running), as vLLM's own tests build it (tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py:641-657@5df63a72); those two methods run unmodified

mocks.symbol: DP wave loop (harness copy of DPEngineCoreProc.run_busy_loop)
mocks.how: oracle/run_dp.py only, and NOT vLLM's code: run_busy_loop (vllm/v1/engine/core.py:2328-2405@5df63a72) blocks on ZMQ queues and a process group, so the harness writes its per-step decisions itself, transcribed from it: a rank that ran nothing while it has unfinished requests or the wave runs executes a dummy batch (:2354-2368); _has_global_unfinished_reqs is skipped on a rank that is idle and not running (:2357-2358); when it returns False the wave number advances and the step counter resets (:2384-2393); and a request reaching a rank whose wave is not running starts every rank's wave at once, a simplification of the FIRST_REQ / START_DP_WAVE round trip through the coordinator (core_client.py:1590-1593, coordinator.py:363-374, core.py:2234-2248, 2281-2298). These are the harness's decisions, so the trace's dummy, waves, running and step_counter fields, and mutants D4-D7, show that blis-vllm matches this transcription, not vLLM's loop itself (docs/testing.md, tier 3)

oracle/run_connector.py only: vLLM's create_vllm_config helper (tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py:111-180@5df63a72) always enables prefix caching, fixes the scheduling policy, the long-prefill cap and the watermark, and builds ModelConfig without the scenario's max_model_len (it reaches SchedulerConfig only, :132-142), while the Scheduler reads model_config.max_model_len (vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:145). So the scenario's values are set on the CacheConfig, SchedulerConfig and ModelConfig after construction and before the Scheduler is built, which reads them at construction, and SchedulerConfig.verify_max_model_len (vllm/config/scheduler.py:314-357), which those edits bypass, is run again on the result

oracle/run_connector.py only: the kv_transfer_params a P/D proxy hands each side (do_remote_prefill and the remote block ids for a decoder, do_remote_decode for a prefiller) are set on the Request as vLLM's own create_request builds them (tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py:246-264@5df63a72); the connector reads them unmodified

oracle/run_offloading.py only: the scenario's VllmConfig is built by vLLM's own config constructors (ModelConfig with the scenario's max_model_len, SchedulerConfig with its policy, long-prefill cap and watermark, CacheConfig with prefix_cache_retention_interval None, dense retention, which core/kv models, and KVTransferConfig naming OffloadingConnector with the scenario's kv_connector_extra_config), the values tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py:111-180@5df63a72 create_vllm_config fixes; the KV cache groups are vLLM's own FullAttentionSpec and SlidingWindowSpec of the scenario's page, each window tagged with extra_retained_tokens as get_kv_cache_configs tags it (vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:2582-2589). The spec is CPUOffloadingSpec (vllm/v1/kv_offload/factory.py:31): TieringOffloadingSpec's scheduler-side manager needs a /dev/shm region (vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/spec.py:342-350) and with no secondary tiers forwards every scheduler call to its CPU primary tier, a CPUOffloadingManager (tiering/manager.py:396-417, 569-661, 736-781, 843-873, 912-921), so a scenario stating it is refused, not substituted. Nothing is written into a built object

oracle/run_offloading.py only: the worker side (OffloadingConnectorWorker, vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/worker.py:40-323@5df63a72) is the transport mock. On each step's OffloadingConnectorMetadata it follows the worker's protocol: jobs_to_flush are submitted and waited for at once (handle_preemptions, :198-224), the stores the previous step deferred and this step's loads are submitted (start_kv_transfers, :226-238) and this step's stores are deferred to the next step (prepare_store_kv, :240-249). A submitted load completes load_delay steps later and a store store_delay steps later (the scenario's, per request or for all). Completions reach the scheduler as vLLM's own OffloadingWorkerMetadata(completed_jobs={job: 1}) (offloading/common.py:76-104) in the step's KVConnectorOutput.kv_connector_worker_meta, and a completed load's request in finished_recving (worker.py:273-309); the worker reports both as sets, so the mock fixes their order: jobs by job id, requests by request id. The Go side (core/connector/offloading) reports them in the same order

oracle/run_offloading.py only: the Scheduler's finished_req_ids is a set of request-id strings (vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:237, 2736), and str hashing is randomised per process (python -I ignores PYTHONHASHSEED), so vLLM's own iteration order over it is not reproducible from run to run. OffloadingConnectorScheduler iterates it to store a finished request's last chunks and to tell the CPU manager the request finished (offloading/scheduler.py:1576-1579, 1889-1896@5df63a72), which orders prepare_store (CPU evictions) and the LRU's recency updates when two or more requests finish between steps. Before each schedule() the runner replaces the attribute with a set holding the same ids that iterates in sorted order; membership and size are unchanged and the scheduler reads it only through iteration and membership. The Go side's offloading connector (core/connector/offloading, added after this mock) iterates the step's finished requests in the same sorted request-id order
